title: Banu Hilal migration to the Maghreb
summary: The Fatimid caliph in Cairo invited the Bani Hilal and Bani Salim, Bedouin tribes from Arabia, to move west to the Maghrib and punish the Zirids, who had broken with the Fatimids in 1049. One archaeological review dates the invasion of the region to 1051. They devastated Cyrenaica and Tripolitania and sacked Tripoli; the Bani Salim seem to have stopped in Libya, while the Bani Hilal continued to the Atlantic coast of Morocco.

uncertainty.note: King (1989): the Bani Hilal and Bani Sulaym invaded the region in 1051. LOC: the Zirid amir broke with the Fatimids in 1049. LOC gives no year for the invitation or the later stages, and the path is undated. The id says 1050.

beats.caption: The Zirid amir rejects the Shia creed and breaks with the Fatimids; the caliph in Cairo responds by inviting the Hilalian tribes west.
The Bani Hilal and Bani Sulaym invade the region, sweeping across Cyrenaica and Tripolitania; Tripoli is sacked.
The Bani Salim seem to stop in Libya while the Bani Hilal continue to the Atlantic coast of Morocco, completing the Arabization of the region.
